title: Learning Transferable Visual Models From Natural Language Supervision
authors: A. Radford, J. Kim, C. Hallacy, et al. (12 authors)
before: Vision models were trained on fixed label sets like ImageNet's thousand classes.
problem: A fixed vocabulary of labels cannot describe an open world, and collecting labels does not scale.
breakthrough: Train image and text encoders contrastively on 400M web pairs so that matching pairs land together in one space.
why: It created a shared image-text space, the bridge every vision-language model crosses.
next: Flamingo, LLaVA and GPT-4V all use CLIP-style encoders.
inherits: The joint embedding space that lets a language model see.
